definitions.definition: Torus=reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). Periodic spatial products, integrals and derivatives are on this torus. A trigonometric polynomial is a finite sum of exp(i*k*x) with integer k.

For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x)exp(-i*k*x) dx, k in Z. Extend Fourier coefficients to periodic distributions. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0. For sequences, ell^2 is the square-summable sequence space with counting measure.

definitions.type: family of real or complex Hilbert spaces indexed by real order
definitions.definition: Write <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_{k in Z}<k>^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2, interpreted as distributions for s<0. L^2=H^0 and ||.||_2 denotes its normalized norm. For mean-zero f, ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2. For s>=0, ||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s); for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s). In time L^infty norms are essential suprema, replaced by ordinary suprema for continuous representatives; derivative norms remain essential suprema.

definitions.type: one-parameter family of linear Fourier operators
definitions.definition: For real t, S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3) has Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3).
P0 f=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
P=identity-P0, where identity is the identity linear operator.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at zero. Write Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). Spatial differentiation partial_x has multiplier i*k.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)]. Initially use smooth inputs; the negative Sobolev extension to L^2 inputs is proved below.

For I=[a,b], C_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))}dt. Constant inputs are identified with constant time paths. At smooth inputs this is an ordinary integral, and the source estimates supply its continuous extensions.

definitions.type: family of bilinear integrated quadratic stages
definitions.definition: For a base time a>=0, step tau>0, t in [a,a+tau], and constant mean-zero inputs f,g, F_a(t;f,g)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(f,g)ds. Abbreviate F_a(t;f)=F_a(t;f,f). Its endpoint representation and extensions are proved below.

output.statement: There is an absolute C>0 such that the following bounds hold uniformly in time. For mean-zero f,g in L^2 and all real t, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(fg)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 whenever the latter is finite; ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2. For all A,A2 in H^1, the algebra bound is: ||A*A2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality/mean and is strongly continuous. For continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Also J_t is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). In particular F_a(t;f,g)=[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/6 for constant inputs. All bounded product maps extend from polynomials by density.

argument.text: For arbitrary mean-zero L^2 input f, Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<=(sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2 and ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. More generally H^1 embeds into L^infty by the summability of <k>^(-2). For A,A2 in H^1, ||AA2||_2<=||A||_infinity||A2||_2 and partial_x(AA2)=A' A2+A A2', giving ||AA2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). These first hold for polynomials and extend by completeness. Since S_t is an isometry on H^s by its modulus-one multiplier, this proves ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. S_t also preserves reality and zero mode. Strong continuity follows by dominated convergence in the weighted square-summable Fourier series.

produces.statement: For all mean-zero L^2 inputs, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2 and ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For A,A2 in H^1, ||AA2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary and strongly continuous on every H^s and preserves reality and mean.

argument.text: For L^2 functions F,G, the convolution coefficient satisfies |hat(FG)(k)|<=||F||_2||G||_2. Thus ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2*sum_(k!=0)k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), which is finite since pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound and sum k^(-2)<infinity give ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1) gives ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. Finally, in J_t(A,g), bound S_t Dinv A in L^2 and S_t Dinv g in L^infty using F001, proving the asymmetric estimate. These bounds justify the stated bounded extensions by polynomial density.

produces.statement: For mean-zero L^2 inputs ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2; for arbitrary L^2 inputs FF,GG, ||Dinv P(FF*GG)||_2<=C||FF||_2||GG||_2. For mean-zero A with Dinv A in L^2, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 and ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2.

argument.text: Now fix arbitrary continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b] and a third such path h. On k!=0 the coefficient of J_t(f,g) is sum_(r+s=k)exp(-3*i*k*r*s*t)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiation of the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients, so d_t J_t(f,g)=3 B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smoothness gives absolute Fourier convergence for every derivative used. Integrate and divide by three to obtain the normal form, summing over pieces if necessary; continuity makes the internal endpoints cancel. Symmetry is immediate. Because Dinv partial_x=P and S_t commutes with these Fourier multipliers, J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)]*(S_t Dinv h)}. Integrating gives C_I(f,g,h) with no commutation through a product. At constant f,g the derivative terms vanish, giving Stage=[J]_a^t/6. Quantifying the inputs proves the asserted conclusion.
